items.title: Man Drives U-Haul Box Truck 1,200 Miles To Get Home During Nationwide Ground Stop
items.summary:
Last week’s nationwide ground stop threw a heap of chaos into one of the busiest travel seasons of the year, but that wasn’t going to stop Greg Swan from getting home from Dallas to Minneapolis. With all flights canceled, no rental cars available, and no viable train route, Swan grabbed a one-way Chevy Express rental from U-Haul and drove that sucker 1,200 miles home. Where have we seen this before ?

If you think about it, it does make sense; U-Haul’s business is optimized for one-way rentals, after all. And I’m sure most of the nation’s travelers marooned by the FAA’s nationwide ground stop would not think to do that in their desperation to get where they were going.

“It was my Muse AI agent’s idea!” Swan told us. “No flights, rental cars, bus, or train options anywhere. Too much going on at home to play the rebook and cancellation game. But U-Haul had two one-way trucks to choose from! Long drive, but worth it to be home.”

Swan also shared some choice driving impressions. “Also, no cruise control. And a speed governor that wouldn’t let it go faster than 73 mph. And a super strong spring in that accelerator for pushing down on it for 21 hours. My calf is pissed. Belt screaming down the interstate. A miserable driving experience.”

“After 21 hours on the road, Swan dropped his colleague off at the Minneapolis airport at 3:15 a.m. Sunday, before Swan arrived home at 4 a.m.,” News 9 shared.

Greg Swan/X 

Having crossed the country in those box trucks a time or two myself, I say they ain’t that bad! But having to unexpectedly spend three days driving one when you thought…
items.t: Canceled Flight? Try U-Haul. One Desperate Traveller Went 1,200 Miles in an Empty Moving Truck Just To Get Home

items.title: The Aston Martin Dreadnought Is Going Racing for Real, but It Was Born From Call of Duty
items.summary:
Aston Martin is venturing into the exciting world of off-road rally racing , and it’s doing so with a sweet-looking truck: the Aston Martin Dreadnought. Originally conceived as a digital creation for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , the Dreadnought is jumping into the mortal realm to do some serious racing at the 2027 Dakar rally .

This explains why when I first saw these photos on social media, I thought they were merely digital renderings or, as automakers like to call them nowadays, “creative exercises.” The off-roader was legit born as a video game war machine, yet it will go racing in the real world in a few months. Even better yet, Aston kept that steampunk-ness that makes it look like it doesn’t belong in reality. The stance, the bodywork, the livery—it’s all very cool and somewhat resembles a rally-fied Valiant.

Aston Martin 

No performance specs have been released yet, though it’s safe to assume the Dreadnought will not compete against its cross-town rival, the Defender, which races in the Stock class. It’ll most likely be powered by a V8 from the automaker’s stable, but that’s yet to be seen. Furthermore, Aston has chosen the racing experts at Prodrive as its engineering partner, greatly improving the brand’s odds of surviving its first-ever Dakar. 

Last but not least, Aston has hired some serious stars to get behind the wheel of its three machines. Performing driving duty will be two-time Formula 1 champion Fernando Alonso , nine-time World Rally Champion Sébastien Loeb, and reigning World Rally Raid Champion Lucas Moraes.

Aston Martin

items.title: Toyota’s Scion KEI-01 First-Drive Review: A Billy Goat Many People Are Going to Want
items.summary:
Key Takeaways 

Toyota revives Scion with KEI-01. The right-hand-drive Kei truck is legally coming to America, targeting niche markets. 

Unique design and features. Compact size, removable bed sides, and right-hand drive make it stand out. 

Off-road capability shines. The KEI-01 climbs like a billy goat with its 660 cc engine and four-wheel drive. 

Competitive pricing potential. Expected to cost under $30,000, making it an attractive option for fleet buyers. 

Bottom line: Toyota's Scion KEI-01 is a quirky, capable Kei truck poised to capture a unique market with its off-road prowess and competitive pricing. 

✦ 
 AI assisted, editor reviewed 

As you may have heard, Toyota is bringing back Scion, and its first product will be a right-hand-drive Kei truck named KEI-01 . We don’t know much about the KEI-01, but we know what matters: it’s a Kei truck being brought legally to America.

A day after the reveal, I got to drive the KEI-01 on a gravel course to get an initial impression. Here’s what I learned in those few minutes:

A Kei truck is an ultra-compact, purposeful truck built to meet Japan’s keijidōsha (light vehicle) class. Strict size limits keep these things from being wider than 5 feet and no longer than just over 11 feet. They aren’t powerful, they aren’t fancy, and they’re usually extremely capable, especially given their size.

Joel Feder 

The outside looks like a miniature cabover truck you might see in the toy aisle at Target or like someone shrunk a European truck. It’s like nothing on the road here in the U.S. The cab is upright; there’s basically no…
items.t: Toyota’s Scion KEI-01 First-Drive Review: A Billy Goat Many People Are Going to Want

items.title: Toyota’s Scion KEI-01 Kei Truck Will Cost Less Than $30,000—And $22,000 ‘Seems Reasonable’
items.summary:
Last week, something borderline unbelievable happened: Toyota said it would sell a Kei truck in the U.S. market. Actually, two unbelievable things happened, as the automaker also said it would revive the Scion brand from the graveyard.

Questions abound, but from the outset it’s clear Toyota’s Scion KEI-01 truck will be a low-volume affair, at least for now. But what will it cost? Toyota USA’s Vice President of Engineering, Don Federico, told The Drive that “$22,000 seems reasonable” and “It’ll cost less than $30,000.”

As one of the few people who have driven Scion’s KEI-01, I can tell you it’s like a little billy goat, and so many people will want this thing. But maybe not you. No one’s going to be hauling their kid to school or soccer practice in this thing. For the money, a Ford Maverick makes a lot more sense.

But ranchers, hotels, municipalities, and so many other outfits, including small businesses, looking for a little workhorse might be lining up for this thing. Especially for that pricing.

Federico was quick to note it’s really not hard in this day and age to spend $30,000, $35,000, or (and I probably twisted my face when he told me this) up to $45,000 on a utility UTV featuring four-wheel drive, an enclosed cab with both air conditioning and heat, and a radio. What’s more, those more expensive machines don’t come with a bulletproof 660 cc three-cylinder engine, a factory warranty from Toyota, or the ability to be serviced at a Toyota dealership. They dot America like McDonald’s.

As someone who isn’t living in the world of UTVs and small utility vehicles, my…

items.title: Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?
items.summary:
There’s no particularly comfortable way to talk about motorcycle safety. Motorcycles are dangerous. All the statistics point to the fact that per mile, motorcycles are significantly more dangerous. And as someone who promotes them as a better alternative to large cars and trucks for many trips, it’s an uncomfortable reality that must be grappled with.

But that simple statement also hides something important. Not all motorcycles, riders, or riding behaviors carry the same risk. And as a new generation of smaller electric motorcycles begins to emerge, I think there’s an interesting question worth asking: Could electric motorcycles inadvertently make motorcycling safer?

more…
items.t: Motorcycles are notoriously dangerous. Could electric motorcycles actually change that?

items.title: REO Targets 5,000-Pound Max Towing for Its Tiny Four-Cylinder Trucks
items.summary:
Call me cautiously optimistic about REO Industries and the Runabout family of vehicles it hopes to build. They’re still a long way from production, but in theory, they should be pretty sweet. Not only does the startup want to sell its simple trucks for $21,500 and up; it also wants to build them with simple four-cylinder engines, manual transmissions, and mechanical 4×4. And in speaking with REO Founder and CEO Zach De Bernardi, The Drive learned that they could also tow up to 5,000 pounds—quite a bit more than the Ford Maverick.

While flipping through REO’s press photos showing the truck that was styled by Frank Stephenson Design, we noticed a T4X single-cab model pulling a 20-foot fiberglass boat on a tandem-axle trailer. We estimated the weight to be 5,000 pounds or more with a little bit of napkin math, and De Bernardi confirmed that’s the goal. He added that the Toyota Hilux Champ can do 5,500 pounds, so it set the benchmark. Supposedly, the REO Runabout will have larger wheels than the ‘Yota, so it can also fit bigger brakes.

As for payload, REO targets a max capacity of 2,500 pounds. REO Industries 

It’s encouraging to see a startup value such strong fundamentals. REO isn’t interested in small-displacement, big-power turbo engines to compensate for anything. Instead, it seems comfortable embracing less impressive stats if that results in greater dependability—500,000 miles is the goal.

Take, for example, REO’s decision to run a solid axle instead of independent front suspension. “First and foremost, this vehicle is designed as a truck,” De Bernardi told The…
items.t: REO Targets 5,000-Pound Max Towing for Its Tiny Four-Cylinder Trucks

items.title: REO Wants to Fight Ford and Slate With These Oh-So-Simple Work Trucks
items.summary:
I don’t know about you, but I’m glad to be alive for the small truck renaissance we’re enjoying. Don’t get me wrong— I like big trucks as much as the next guy , but even I can admit they aren’t always practical. Ford and Slate are bringing affordable pickups to market in the next few years, but as some people can’t help but hate, they’re both electric. REO might be good news for those folks, though, as the startup promises real-deal trucks on the cheap with naturally aspirated four-cylinder engines, manual transmissions, and solid front axles.

Called the Runabout, this rig comes in three different flavors: the T4X work truck, T4C crew cab, and S4C family SUV. We’ve known about them for a while, but until now, they were just names on paper. REO has since partnered with Frank Stephenson Design—led by the fella who penned the reborn Mini, as well as the McLaren P1—to style its machinery. According to the snazzy sketches REO sent over, the trucks’ exterior is based on a bison. It’s called biomimicry, and it’s everywhere in design. ( For what it’s worth, Frank Stephenson says the sailfish was his main inspo for the P1 .)

REO Industries 

What’s most remarkable about these REO Runabout models is their intentional simplicity. All of them should ride on the same ladder frame, with the same engines, the same mechanical 4×4 systems, and the same transmission options. Now, not all of them will be manuals, but those that are will be about $1,500 cheaper than their self-shifting counterparts. REO’s CEO and Founder, Zach De Bernardi, explained to The Drive that they’re still…

items.title: Ford’s Rouge Facility Was Targeted by Massive Employee-Aided Theft Ring
items.summary:
Ford’s Rouge assembly plant has been identified as one of the sources of parts sold online as part of a multi-year, multi-million-dollar heist operation run by four people (including a Ford employee). The ring was busted last May after tens of thousands of dollars worth of stolen, brand-new parts were identified in the inventory of an eBay storefront. 

The discovery led to raids on warehouses and homes in Detroit and the suburbs of Dearborn and Canton last year. Police were seen recovering entire pallets of OEM parts ranging from body panels to entire axle assemblies. 

Ford’s Rouge Factory in Dearborn was the source of roughly $80,000 in stolen parts , Automotive News reported Monday. Using their employee connection to gain access to the facility, the ring pilfered parts over the course of six consecutive Saturday nights in the spring 0f 2025. 

Rouge was not the only source of stolen inventory. Dearborn Police Chief Issa Shahin told Fox 2 Detroit last May that the thieves also hit Ford facilities in Wayne and Flat Rock over a period of at least two years. The details of those thefts were not included in the latest report. 

During a Nov. 10 news conference, Wayne Country Prosecutor Kym Worthy told media that the total value of the property stolen while the ring was in operation is much larger than what was listed in the charges against the four alleged ringleaders (Badr Kahil, 63, Aiman Kahil, 25, and Firas Kahil, 36, and Wissam Faraj, 35). 

Warehouses in Detroit filled “from the floor to the ceiling” with brand-new Ford parts ranging from body panels, Shahin said.…
items.t: Ford’s Rouge Facility Was Targeted by Massive Employee-Aided Theft Ring

items.title: Mercedes’ Hands-Free Driving Assist Tackled San Fran’s Steepest Streets, Cyclists, Traffic. Here’s How It Went
items.summary:
Back in the summer of 2022, I went to Germany to test Mercedes-Benz’s Level 3 hands-free driving system, and it impressed me then. I could read The Drive while the car drove itself down the road, and even play video games from the center touchscreen. However, the tech was heavily regulated for highway operation only and limited to a paltry 37 mph. Fast forward to last week, and I climbed into a U.S.-spec 2027 Mercedes GLC 400 Electric to see what the brand’s new point-to-point Level 2 hands-free assist could do in a busy metropolis like San Francisco.

Dubbed MB Drive Assist Pro and Hands-Free Highway Assist, these latest tech offerings from Mercedes allow drivers in California to take their hands off the wheel while navigating urban environments and eligible controlled-access highways. And unlike before, you can do it at speeds up to 85 mph.

Mercedes-Benz 

You can watch the video below to see how I fared through the busy streets of the Bay Area, including typical big-city treats like double-parked cars, road construction, cyclists, and, of course, lots of pedestrians. Most impressively, however, was the system’s confidence and fluidity in its decisions, always feeling sure of its movements, which is more I can say for rival systems out there.

MB Drive Assist Pro uses 27 sensing components—including 10 cameras, five radar sensors, and 12 ultrasonic sensors—and a high-performance computer delivering up to 254 Tera Operations Per Second to process the incoming data. As you’ll see in the video, the dual screens (gauge cluster and infotainment) show what the car sees and…
items.t: Mercedes’ Hands-Free Driving Assist Tackled San Fran’s Steepest Streets, Cyclists, Traffic. Here’s How It Went

items.title: Feds Investigate 1 Million Hondas for Auto Stop/Start Trouble: TDS
items.summary:
Good morning and welcome to The Downshift , a daily sweep of today’s top headlines from the auto industry and car culture, curated by The Drive’s editorial team. Each story gets a short summary and a link to the original source if you want to dive deeper.

Here’s what’s cooking on Monday, November 16, 2026:

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into 2024-2026 model year Honda Odyssey, Passport, Ridgeline, and Pilot vehicles, plus the Acura MDX, for auto stop/start engine problems. That’s over 1 million cars in total, and, to date, 700 owners have complained that their cars’ engines have not fired up again in traffic after shutting off. Regulators were already looking into some recent Honda vehicles reportedly exhibiting this behavior, but this particular group does not appear to share their root cause, and the same repairs don’t seem to apply. [ Reuters ] 

BMW is recalling more than 720,000 vehicles across a range of nameplates for short-circuit-prone water pumps that could cause fires. The automaker actually issued a recall for this two years ago, but the fix apparently didn’t take, and it’s once again recommending that owners park away from structures and other cars. All the affected vehicles are from model years 2012 through 2018, and the 3 Series, 5 Series, X3, X4, and X5 are included, as well as others; follow the following link for the complete list.
